item.title: Judge orders Texas voucher program deadline be extended amid controversy over exclusion of Islamic schools
item.description: Texas had excluded schools over alleged ties to CAIR, the nation’s largest Muslim advocacy group. The ruling adds to scrutiny over how the state evaluated applicants. The post Judge orders Texas voucher program deadline be extended amid controversy over exclusion of Islamic schools appeared first on District Administration.

item.title: How Ohio schools teach COVID, 6 years later
item.description: How schools teach COVID still varies, and early research suggests textbooks often treat it in fragmented ways. In Ohio, some teachers use the pandemic to help students connect recent events to broader history.

item.title: Cursive is back. But should students be learning the skill?
item.description: Cursive is making a comeback in schools, but experts disagree on its value. Supporters see benefits for spelling and engagement, while critics say class time may be better spent on other skills.

item.title: Could breaking up the Education Department actually improve federal education policy?
item.description: A new commentary says some education programs might work better outside the Education Department, but splitting them up could also make federal policy harder to coordinate.

item.title: Opinion: AI makes human writing more valuable—and changes how schools should teach it
item.description: AI may be increasing the value of strong human writing, prompting calls for schools to teach students to write both independently and with AI tools. Writing and editing skills could become more important as AI-generated content becomes more common.

item.title: Conservative parents and teachers unions become unlikely allies fighting tech in schools
item.description: After years of maligning teachers unions, Moms for Liberty has joined forces with its former adversaries to push for limits on laptops in classrooms.

item.title: Portland Public Schools shortens school year in budget-cutting agreement with teachers union
item.description: Portland Public Schools is turning four days that were originally intended for instruction, grading or paid time off into furlough days.

item.title: Wisconsin school board races get big boost in spending from national conservative group
item.description: Records show some candidates were hand-picked by 1776 Project PAC, a national conservative political group that spent more than $160,000 this spring on local public school board races.

item.title: Georgia high school students will no longer be able to use cellphones in class
item.description: Supporters of a recent Georgia bill to limit student cellphone use during the school day say it would reduce distractions and improve safety, while some students worry it could make communication harder during emergencies.

item.title: Texas Education Agency orders public schools to remove mentions of Cesar Chavez from lessons
item.description: Schools were also directed to cancel or change celebrations of the late civil rights leader amid allegations of sexual abuse.
